newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Aug 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Aug 18.

text.p: CHE plan to slash mental health care: Capital Coast Health wants its loss-making mental health services set up as a stand-alone business and most patients dealt with by family doctors, according to a leaked draft business plan. Page 1.
Bill aims to recognise wills from same-sex relationships: A proposed law recognising homosexual relationships is being hailed as a breakthrough for homosexual and lesbian rights. Page 1.

Prebble unfazed by Quigley comments: ACT NZ leader Richard Prebble believes there is little likelihood of his fellow MP and party co-founder Derek Quigley leaving ACT to shore up the coalition's majority. Page 2.

Companies looting tax base, says Delamere: Both the government's Treasury ministers are on a collision course with the business sector after Tuariki Delamere accused big corporations on Sunday of looting New Zealand's tax base. Page 3.
Reserve Bank tipped to sanction easing: ANZ Bank predicts that the Reserve Bank will allow monetary conditions to ease as much as about 75 points on the monetary conditions index. Page 13.
Flat first-quarter profit expected for Telecom: Telecom is expected to produce flat first-quarter earnings when it reports on Tuesday. Page 13.

Power NZ eyes $38m offer for WEL stake: The directors of Power NZ plan to consult their company's main shareholders before deciding whether they will accept a $38 million offer for the company's ten percent stake in Hamilton power supplier WEL Energy. Page 14.
Power firms 'milk' $150m: Electricity prices in New Zealand have raced ahead of inflation as energy retailers make undue profits on the back of consumers, a watchdog group says.
Crash survivor calm as jet 'torn to bits': Guam crash survivor Barry Small experienced no fear or pain as he calmly watched a jumbo jet disintegrate and explode around him.
Battle of wills may be over for children: Adult children may soon be blocked from contesting a parent's will to get a bigger share of the inheritance.

Less scope for firms to avoid paying tax: Incentives for companies to invest a lot of time and resources in tax minimisation have been greatly reduced, compared with the winebox era of the late 1980s.

Move for cheaper calls 'may fail': United States efforts to force other countries to slash the rates they charge for incoming phone calls could prove toothless in the face of the complexities of the international calls market, the general manager of Telecom's network marketing, Tony Briscoe, says.
Winebox surveyed: This week's Business Herald/University of Auckland survey will test reaction to the recommendations of Winebox Commissioner Sir Ronald Davison -- specifically those on taxation.
BP looks to food link to lift petrol sales: BP Oil New Zealand is negotiating alliance with supermarkets and fast-food outlets to increase its retail sales of petrol
